1#_: And if it is a doubt. See She'elat Yaavetz part 1 siman 218, where he elaborated whether the rule that an important item is not nullified is from the Torah or only d'rabbanan — see there.
2#_: Such as nevelah. See in the responsa of Mahari Halevi siman 25, who wrote that even when it became nevelah through death it is worthy of honor. He further wrote that even if it is very lean it is worthy of honor — see there.
3#_: And basar b'chalav. See in the responsa of Noda BiYehudah Yoreh Deah siman 64 regarding an incident where they baked kreplach with butter in nine copper pots, and within them were two in which kreplach had previously been baked with fat; and he wrote that although they greased the molds with fat and butter and it was visible, and therefore the whole became forbidden, nevertheless they are nullified in the majority, for those baked in the two are the minority against the remainder, and they are nullified as the law of dry-with-dry; and it is not called a piece worthy of honor, for although in basar b'chalav it is a prohibition on account of itself, nevertheless here the main substance is the dough, and basar b'chalav is absorbed — therefore it is nullified; one need only forbid according to the number of those baked in the two molds and permit the rest. And one could say it is considered not in its kind, for fat is not the same kind as butter, and sixty is required even in dry, and even for an absorbed prohibition, because if they cook them it will impart taste; nevertheless here it was only a d'rabbanan prohibition, for all the fat was goose fat, and in such a case the Shach wrote in siman 109 that even not in its kind is nullified in dry one against two — see there.
4#_: In its feathers. See in the responsa of Noda BiYehudah Yoreh Deah siman 16, who wrote that a piece that was not deveined does not have the status of worthy of honor because there is trouble involved; and what is worthy for a non-Jew is not called a piece worthy of honor — nevertheless he did not decide this for absolute permission, but combined this reasoning as one branch with other reasons — see there. [And see in the responsa of Chatam Sofer siman 91, who wrote that a large piece, and also a live animal — we have Rashba, Ran, and Raah, and in my humble opinion the Rambam also holds like Raah, and so ruled the Mechaber, and the Rama only cites that there are those who disagree and wrote that so is the custom; and Peri Chadash fully agrees with the Mechaber — therefore in Frankfurt I added another leniency where there was some doubt whether the needle came out alive through both sides, for after rinsing in hot water a taste was almost sensed on the second side; I relied on the above and permitted with great loss of hundreds — see there.]
5#_: And even though after it was mixed they removed it. See in the responsa of Radbaz (new responsa) siman 267, who wrote that if the tereifah was not found until after it became worthy of honor, it is not nullified — see further there.
6#_: Other intestinal organs. Beit Yosef in the name of Taz regarding goose meat on the breast, etc.; and see Peri Chadash who disagrees and inclined to be lenient like Rashal; however in Bechor Shor in his novellae on Chullin daf 100 he inclined to be stringent like the Taz — see there.
7#_: Fixing. See in the responsa of Shemesh Tzedakah Yoreh Deah siman 33, who challenged that the Mechaber's words contradict one another — for here and in the next seif it implies they are not similar prohibitions, whereas here it deals with whole sheep; also the chicken appears to deal when it is alive, for after cooking one cannot remove the fat; whereas above seif 3 the Mechaber wrote that it is not considered worthy of honor unless it is cooked, and likewise a whole sheep, etc. — see there; he offers many resolutions to this.
